abstract: Open data policies and data sharing in the metabolomics field continue to increase. MetaboLights (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights) is a global, open-access data repository for metabolomics and related fields such as lipidomics and exposomics, hosting experimental data and associated metadata across species, methodologies, and domains. Here we describe significant developments in MetaboLights over the past 3 years to improve data submission, access, and discovery, and strengthen integration of public metabolomics data with other omics data types. As of September 2026, the number of completed submissions to MetaboLights reached ~6900, and of those ~3400 were publicly released. Overall, 91% of datasets were generated using mass spectrometry and 7% using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. A new submission workflow has been introduced along with significant improvements in infrastructure, such as a new data transfer protocol for very large datasets (Globus), a new home page, and an automated study validation framework, among others. We also describe current trends in reuse of MetaboLights datasets and in the field as a whole. Finally, we outline future plans towards better data submission and metadata capture, the coordination with other metabolomics data resources through MetabolomicsHub, and the planned activities related to AI (artificial intelligence).
